messages:
jason: Heads-up — sales looped me in: BetaCorp wants tight latency for their realtime QA feature. Product is pushing for p95 <= 120ms at 50 qps for short prompts. Sales routed a p99 ask too (<= 350ms) for compliance. Can runtime estimate if we can hit those without Dedicated?

maya: quick thought: p95 120ms is already tough on hosted with our current microbatching + fused-attn kernel when KV cold. p99 350ms maybe feasible if we control caching and avoid kernel swaps. Need profiling. :thinking:

henry: pinging perf-bot for recent perf numbers on 8B model with typical BetaCorp prompt lengths (<=64 tokens) and sequence len distribution.

perf-bot: profiling results attached (latest prod run @ host-3):
```
workload: 50 qps, 64-token prompts, model: open-8b-fused
metrics:
  p50: 28ms
  p95: 135ms
  p99: 420ms
  tail (99.9): 1200ms
observations:
  - KV cache hit-rate: 62% during steady phase, drops to ~18% after 30s idle bursts
  - kernel_switch events: 0.6% of requests, add ~120-200ms
  - microbatch sizes avg: 3.8 (target microbatch cap = 8)
```

maya: so our p95 is 135ms not 120, p99 420ms > 350. Major contributors: KV warmup and occasional kernel switches.

sophie: can we tune microbatch cap down to reduce queuing? Sales worried about cost if we throttle throughput.

henry: tradeoffs: lowering microbatch cap from 8->2 reduces queuing latency (p95 drops ~25ms in bench) but throughput per-GPU drops ~18% and cost per request rises. Also worse amortization of kernel overhead.

jason: product will accept slight throughput hit if it guarantees p95 target for SLA. Sales wants to know cost delta. alex-sales: can you summarize constraints for BetaCorp (SLA windows, commit level)?

alex-sales: BetaCorp will pay more for predictable latency but they want hosted first. They prefer not to go Dedicated for initial rollout. Budget allows ~20% premium.

maya: options we should present: 
- Option A (latency-first): Microbatch cap = 2, aggressive KV pinning (prefix caching), pre-warm flows for their endpoints, prefer single optimized kernel (disable runtime kernel swap). Expect p95 ~110-125ms, p99 ~300-380ms. Throughput capacity per GPU -18% -> price + ~22%.
- Option B (cost-balanced): Microbatch cap = 4, keep kernel swap allowed, enable KV background warmers, p95 ~130-150ms, p99 ~380-480ms. Throughput -8% -> price + ~10%.
- Option C (throughput-first): Microbatch cap = 8, full batching, p95 ~140-170ms, p99 >500ms, cost minimal.

henry: technical notes: kernel swap causes large tail due to JIT-style fallback and unmapped fused kernels. We can add a per-route kernel pin to avoid dynamic selection for BetaCorp endpoints. That adds maintenance risk (tests for every model config) but reduces ~120-200ms in tails.

perf-bot: benchmark diff (microbatch cap 8 -> 2, pinned kernel):
```
scenario: short prompts, 50 qps
cap=8, kernel=auto -> p95 135, p99 420, cost_index=1.0
cap=2, kernel=pinned -> p95 112, p99 305, cost_index=1.22
```

jason: good. Next steps: craft two proposals for Sales/Product: latency-guarantee (Option A) and balanced (Option B). Include explicit cost uplift and operational caveats (need prewarm jobs, risk of kernel regressions disabled).

sophie: also add an escape hatch: route to a smaller quantized variant on spikes (fallback model), keeps tail bounded without huge cost. We can support that in rollout.

alex-sales: BetaCorp will likely accept Option A if we can justify cost + show p99 improvement via prewarm + pinned kernel. Can we provide a 2-week pilot SLA with telemetry?

maya: yes we can do a time-limited pilot. We'll need a small dedicated prewarm fleet for their endpoints (not full Dedicated), and a rollout plan: canary -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%. Add tracing hooks and alerting on KV hit-rate <50% or kernel_switch >0.2%.

henry: ops checklist for pilot:
1) create prewarm worker group with pinned kernel image
2) set microbatch cap=2 for the route
3) enable prefix/KV pinning and background warmers
4) add regression eval harness to CI for the pinned kernel
5) instrument trace events for kernel_switch and kv_miss

jason: can you estimate the infra delta and draft the SOW? aim to send to Sales by EOD tomorrow.

henry: infra delta estimate: +2.3 GPUs steady (for 50 qps target at cap=2) vs baseline; extra cost ~ +24% run cost. Will write numbers.

perf-bot: reminder: we saw an unrelated perf regression last week in matmul-opt-v2 that raised p95 by ~8ms across models; confirm regression not impacting BetaCorp route before pilot.

maya: I'll run a quick canary test tomorrow morning against matmul-opt-v2 and report.

deploy-bot: deploy started by maya for canary-job/matmul-check at 2026-03-18T09:12Z :rocket:

jason: thanks team. I'll draft negotiation points for Sales/Product: state that p95 SLA 120ms is achievable with Option A + pilot + 20-25% price uplift; p99 target 350ms is borderline but achievable with kernel pin + prewarm + fallback model. Include timeline and risk bullets.

alex-sales: perfect — I'll sync with the customer and push for pilot. :thumbsup:

maya: note: we should log this config as BetaCorp route in console so Optimize can give future tuning suggestions.

henry: logging + alerts + eval harness PR queued.

jason: closing loop — follow-ups: maya: canary tests tomorrow. henry: infra estimate + checklist. perf-bot: confirm matmul regression status. alex-sales: customer sync. We'll reconvene after canary results.
